posts.author: HoloM
posts.content_md: Can anyone give me more information about the "Cheshire Cat" Hologram, which is printed in Graham Saxby's Book "Practical Holography". It show a cat sitting on a tree, if you move sideways, you see only the tree and the mouth of the cat. Who has made this hologram, and when?

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: This probably is not the information you are looking for, but I used to make 2 channel rainbow masters for a company. We has one channel as the background. It was a litho adhered to a ground glass plate such that we could back light it and at the same time we dropped the lighting to the object thus creating a silloette of the object with the illumintated background. For the second channel we dropped the backgound lighting and illuminated the object. The effect in the final hologram was a displacement of the rainbow colors of the object and background as each slit was about two inches wide or so, side by side.

posts.author: Dinesh
posts.content_md:
[quote:ce971a0a11="linkman_11"]I have made hologams with a few cinderblocks, a tray of sand and a diode laser[/quote:ce971a0a11]

So have most of the people who post here. Unfortunately I haven't read the latest edition of Saxby but I'm pretty sure you're describing an extreme situation. You can make a hologram on a door supported by inner tubes and a diode laser. Making a hologram is pretty easy! You can even make a hologram with an LED on your kitchen table if the object is flat and stuck onto the plate. Making a good hologram - now there's another question

posts.author: linkman_11
posts.content_md: I guess you're right... The holograms are o.k..... Making a good hologram is a different story. Saxby explains how to make a hologram in great detail and the book is a great reference.
